headline: Variance requests for nine properties, including 710 Montgomery Street and 500 Second Street, plus a rehearing request for 26 Titus Avenue.
summary: Nine zoning variance requests are on the agenda, including a drive-through restaurant at 500 Second Street. A rehearing request for a townhouse project at 26 Titus Avenue is also listed.
items: Tabled case ZBA2026-086, 710 Montgomery Street: side yard setback variances to subdivide a lot with a three-family dwelling
ZBA2026-097, 4 Vinton Street: variances for a 33.3 SF sign that is larger than allowed and extends above the roofline
ZBA2026-098, 545 Laurel Street: variances to keep an expanded parking area with a wider driveway and more front yard pavement
ZBA2026-099, 59 Johnson Street: variances to rebuild and expand a side entrance porch with reduced side yard setbacks
ZBA2026-100, 500 Second Street: variances for a drive-through restaurant on a corner lot
ZBA2026-101, 298 Queen City Avenue: variances to convert about 3,600 SF of a hotel into a restaurant
ZBA2025-102, 423 Youville Street: side yard setback variance for an 812 SF second-floor addition
ZBA2026-103, Arbutus Lane, Tax Map 218, Lots 11, 14, and 16: variances for a two-family dwelling on a lot narrower than required
ZBA2026-104, 20 South Main Street: variance to establish a veterinary services use in about 3,000 SF of commercial space
Rehearing request for ZBA2026-063, 26 Titus Avenue: townhouse project that received variances on September 10, 2026
location: City Hall, Third Floor, Aldermanic Chambers, One City Hall Plaza, Manchester, New Hampshire 03101

CITY OF MANCHESTER ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT PUBLIC HEARING AND 
LIMITED BUSINESS MEETING AGENDA 
Thursday, November 12, 2026, 6:00 PM 
City Hall, Third Floor, Aldermanic Chambers 
I. Call to Order 
The Chairman calls the meeting to order and introduce s the Zoning Board Members and City 
Staff. 
II. Public Hearing 
A. Tabled Cases 
1) ZBA2026-086, 710 Montgomery Street 
MX-1 Zoning District, Ward 11 
Brett Allard, Esq.  (Agent) proposes to subdivide the lot where proposed Lot 15 will 
remain improved with a three-family dwelling with a 3.66’ minimum side yard setback 
where 5 ’ is required, and with a combined side yard setback of 15.6 ’ where 20 ’ is 
required, in the MX-1 Zoning District, and seeks a variance from Section(s) 5.3.1.C.3.D 
Minimum Combined Side Yard Setback, and 5.3.1.C.3.E Minimum Setback of One Side 
of the Zoning Ordinance of the City of Manchester, New Hampshire as per documents 
submitted through October 20, 2026. 
B. Current Cases 
2) ZBA2026-097, 4 Vinton Street 
BC-2 Zoning District, Ward 9  
Jay Parillo (Agent) proposes to install a 33.3 SF sign where 25.6 SF is allowed and with 
the sign extending above the roofline by 9” , in the BC-2 Zoning District, and seek s a 
variance from Section(s) 9.6-A Non-Residential Building Sign Standards and 9.8.5.A.3 
Wall Sign Standards of the Zoning Ordinance of the City of Manchester, New Hampshire 
as per documents submitted through September 28, 2026. 
3) ZBA2026-098, 545 Laurel Street 
MX-1 Zoning District, Ward 4 
Josip Sovic proposes to maintain an expanded parking area with a driveway width of 32’ 
where 24’ is allowed, with pavement 3’ from the side lot line where 4’ is required and 
with 75% lot coverage in the front yard where 25% is allowed , in the MX-1 Zoning 
District, and seeks a variance from Section(s) 7.4.2.A Driveway Width, 7.5.1.A.1 Parking

Setbacks, and 5.3.1.A.7.B Maximum Front Yard Impervious Area  of the Zoning 
Ordinance of the City of Manchester, New Hampshire as per documents submitted 
through October 1, 2026. 
4) ZBA2026-099, 59 Johnson Street 
R-2 Zoning District, Ward 7 
John Carboneau (Agent) proposes to reconstruct and expand a side entrance porch with 
new rear facing stairs, and where the proposed roof extends over the front facing stairs, 
with a 3.5’ minimum side yard setback on one side where 5’ is required and a combined 
side yard setback of 12.5’ whe re 20’ is required, in the R-2 Zoning District, and seeks a 
variance from Section(s) 5.3.1.A.3.E Minimum Side Yard Setback One Side, and 
5.3.1.A.3.D Minimum Combined Side Yard Setback Both Sides of the Zoning Ordinance 
of the City of Manchester, New Hampshire as per documents submitted through 
October 8, 2026. 
5) ZBA2026-100, 500 Second Street 
BC-2 Zoning District, Ward 10 
Cory DuBois (Agent) propose to construct a drive -through restaurant on a corner lot 
with a front yard setback of 65’ along Queen City Ave., a street yard setback of 80’ along 
Second St. and a street yard setback of 32 .5’ along Woodbury Ave. Extension, where a 
maximum front/street yard setback of 25’ is allowed in all three instances, with a side 
yard setback of 9.4’ where a minimum of 10’ is required, where the principal front 
entrance does not face the principal frontag e, with transparency on the first floor 
primary façade (Queen City Ave.) of 36%  where 70% is required, with transparency on 
the first floor secondary façades (Woodbury Ave. Ext. and Second St.)  of 31% and 8%, 
respectively, where 40% is required in each i nstance, with a blank wall of 27’ on the 
primary façade where 15’ is allowed and with blank walls of 35’ and 34’ on the 
respective secondary façades where 30’ is allowed, with two dumpsters located in the 
front yard enclosed by an 8’ fence where 4’ is allowed, with a transformer located in the 
street yard and where the Type 2 buffer yard is not maintained for the required 10’ and 
does not contain the required number of shade trees and shrubs , in the BC-2 Zoning 
District, and seek a variance from Section(s) 5.3.1.N.3.C Maximum Front/Street Yard 
Setback (3 counts), 5.3.1.N.3.F Minimum Side Yard Setback, 5.3.1.N.6.C Principal 
Entrance Location, 5.3.1.N.6.A First Story Primary Façade Transparency, 5.3.1.N.6.A 
First Story Secondary Façade Transparency (2 counts),  5.6.5.D Dumpster Location, 
8.2.4-A Fence Height, 5.3.1.N.7.F Utility Location, and  8.2.4 -A Type 2 Buffer Yard  of 
the Zoning Ordinance of the City of Manchester, New Hampshire as per documents 
submitted through October 15, 2026. 
6) ZBA2026-101, 298 Queen City Avenue 
BC-2 Zoning District, Ward 10 
Cory DuBois (Agent)  proposes to convert approximately 3,600 SF of space within an 
existing hotel to new restaurant, where improvements will result in an increase in lot 
coverage from 84.7% to 85.5% where 75% is allowed, with five new parking spaces to

Coverage, 7.5.2.A.1 Parking Setbacks, and 8.1.3.B Type 2 Buffer Yard  of the Zoning

7) ZBA2025-102, 423 Youville Street 
R-2 Zoning District, Ward 12 
Michael Sylvester, Jr. (Agent)  proposes to construct second -floor addition 
approximately 812 SF in size with no expansion of the existing foot print with a 
combined side yard setback of 19.7’ where 20’ is required , in the R-2 Zoning District, 
and seek s a variance from Section(s) 5.3.1.A.3.D Minimum Combined Side Yard 
Setback of the Zoning Ordinance of the City of Manchester, New Hampshire as per 
documents submitted through October 20, 2026. 
8) ZBA2026-103, Arbutus Lane, Tax Map 218, Lots 11, 14, and 16 
R-1A Zoning District, Ward 8 
Joseph Wichert (Agent) proposes to construct a two-family dwelling on a lot with 70’ of 
lot width where 150’ is required, and with a proposed driveway 13’ away from an 
existing driveway on the same lot where 30’ is required, in the R-1A Zoning District, and 
seeks a variance from Section(s) 4.3-A.1.B Two-Family Dwelling, 6.2-B.A Minimum Lot 
Width, 7.4.3.B Distance Between Driveways  of the Zoning Ordinance of the City of 
Manchester, New Hampshire as per documents submitted through October 23, 2026. 
9) ZBA2026-104, 20 South Main Street 
BC-1 Zoning District, Ward 10 
Eli Leino, Esq. (Agent) proposes to establish a veterinary services use in approximately 
3,000 SF of commercial space, in the BC-1 Zoning District and seeks a variance from 
Section(s) 4.3-A.6.AD Veterinary Service s of the Zoning Ordinance of the City of 
Manchester, New Hampshire as per documents submitted through October 29, 2026. 
III. Business Meeting 
A. Requests for Rehearing 
10) ZBA2026-063, 26 Titus Avenue 
R-1B Zoning District, Ward 9 
Nickolas Levasseur requests a rehearing of case ZBA2026-063, where variances were 
granted on September 10, 2026, to construct two townhouse dwellings, one with eight 
units and the other with five units for a total of 13 multifamily dwelling units, on a lot 
with 49,484 SF where 78,000 SF is required, where both buildings are three stories in 
height where 2.5 stories is allowed and both buildings have a height of 38’ where 35’ is 
allowed, and where the parking area for the eight -unit building is within 20’ of the
